deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. This page belongs to Gauss's 1805-06 work on the comet of 1772. That comet (Montaigne/Messier, March-April 1772) was later identified as Biela's comet. Gauss and others suspected it was identical with Pons's comet of November 1805. To fit an orbit to the 1772 observations, each observation needs the Sun's geocentric longitude and the Earth-Sun distance at that instant. This page computes both from solar tables for the 1st and 2nd observations; the next page does the 3rd and 4th.

HEADER. 'Schiefe der Ekliptik scheinbare d. 31 März': apparent obliquity of the ecliptic, eps = 23°28'2.83", needed later to convert the comet's right ascension and declination to ecliptic coordinates.

TIME REDUCTION (obs. 1).
- Observed time: 1772 March 26, 8h25'33".
- Add +5'28.9". This is the equation of time (apparent to mean), which is about +5.5 min at the end of March.
- Add +33'35". This is the longitude difference Paris to Seeberg (Seeberg is 42m56s east of Greenwich, Paris 9m21s), so the tables are referred to the Seeberg meridian, as in von Zach's solar tables (my identification).
- Result: 9h4'36.9" mean Seeberg time.
- Decimal form: 4'36.9" = 4.615', so t = 9.076917 h. Then 9.076917/24 = 0.378205, giving 'März 26,378205'.

MEAN LONGITUDE (obs. 1), in signs.degrees.minutes.seconds:
- Epoch 1772: 9s10°38'55.44" = 280°38'55.44".
- Plus motion for the days to March 26: 2s23°46'48.07" = 83°46'48.07".
- Plus motion for 9.077 h: 22'21.98".
- Sum = 364°48'5.49", i.e. 4°48'5.49" (mod 360).

TABLE ARGUMENTS (obs. 1).
- One column is an argument in 1/10000 of a circle: 5045.78 + 2327.07 + 10.37 = 7383.22. Its rate of about 27.38 per day equals 10000/365.26, so it is the solar anomaly argument (my identification).
- Four perturbation arguments in 1/1000 of a circle, each summed mod 1000:
  - 869+878+13 = 760; rate about 34/day, so the Moon.
  - 613+146+1 = 760; rate about 1.5-1.7/day, so Venus.
  - 412+213+1 = 626; rate about 2.5/day, so Jupiter.
  - 404+13 = 417; very slow, so the lunar node / nutation argument.

EQUATION OF CENTRE (side calculation). Table value 1°55'16.290" + 1.965" (interpolation) + 5.207" (a constant correction that recurs as 5.21-5.22 on every observation) = 1°55'23.46".

TRUE LONGITUDE (obs. 1). 4°48'5.49" + 1°55'23.46" = 6°43'28.95". Then add the table corrections:
- Moon -7.48".
- Venus -5.60".
- Jupiter +7.64".
- A term of +28.96" tied to the node argument 417, probably nutation plus aberration plus the tables' constant.
Result: Long. Sun = 6°43'52.45". An earlier value, 46.82", is cancelled.

RADIUS VECTOR (obs. 1).
- Table value R0 = 0.9990494 (read from the overwritten figure).
- Corrections in units of 1e-7: Moon -23+4, Venus -183, Jupiter -115 (overwritten from -135).
- R = 0.9990177; log R = 9.9995732 (i.e. -0.0004268).
- The cancelled values 0.9990050 and 9.999564 are a first attempt.

OBS. 2.
- Time: 8h16'42" + 5'10.3" (corrected from 5'49") + 33'35" = 8h55'27.3". Decimal: 8h55.455' = 8.924250 h; /24 gives 'März 27,371844'.
- Mean longitude: 280°38'55.44" + 84°45'56.40" + 21'59.42" = 5°46'51.26". The day increment 84°45'56.40" - 83°46'48.07" = 59'8.33" is the mean daily motion; 21'59.42" is the motion in 8.924 h.
- Arguments: 5045.78 + 2354.45 + 10.19 = 7410.42. Perturbation arguments 794, 761, 629, 417 (each sum checks mod 1000).
- Equation of centre: 1°55'21.70" + 1.75" + 5.21" = 1°55'28.66".
- True longitude: 7°42'19.92" with corrections -7.21, -5.54, +7.74, +28.96 gives Long. Sun = 7°42'43.89".
- Radius vector: tabular 0.9992269 plus interpolation 1098.9 - 2.9 = 1096 (with 1054.6 + 42.2 + 2.1 = 1098.9 as the difference scheme) gives 0.9993365. Corrections +104 +4 -183 -110 give R = 0.9993180, log R = 9.9997037. The cancelled value 9.9996980 was a first attempt.

UNRESOLVED SCRATCH. The top-right figures (216+23=239, 822, 478, 458, 18.75, 27.75, 208) and 149.67+19 → 1.68 are unresolved interpolation scratch.

CONSISTENCY CHECK (mine). Between the two observations (0.9936 d) the radius vector increases by 0.000287. This matches dR/dt ≈ e n sin M ≈ 0.000287/day. The solar longitude advances 58'51". Both values are plausible for late March 1772.
errors: Obs. 1 longitude: 6°43'28.95" - 7.48 - 5.60 + 7.64 + 28.96 = 6°43'52.47", but Gauss writes 52.45" (0.02" off). The Moon term is overwritten; if it reads -7.50 the sum is exact.

Obs. 2 longitude: 7°42'19.92" - 7.21 - 5.54 + 7.74 + 28.96 = 7°42'43.87", but Gauss writes 43.89" (0.02" off). This is either a misread digit or a small unrecorded term; it is negligible for comet work.

Obs. 1 radius vector: the sum is consistent only if the last correction is -115, not -135 as first written. The cancelled 0.9990050 and 9.999564 show Gauss caught and corrected an arithmetic or table slip.
Obs. 2 equation of time: 5'49" was first written and corrected to 5'10.3". The mean time 8h55'49" was likewise corrected to 8h55'27.3".
All other additions, the mod-360 and mod-1000 reductions, the time-to-decimal-day conversions and the log conversions check correctly.

results.what: Reduction of apparent Paris time of comet observations to mean Seeberg time and decimal day: equation of time plus the meridian difference of 33m35s.
results.modern_name: Time reduction (apparent to mean solar time, meridian transfer)

results.what: Computation of the Sun's true longitude (Long. Sun 6°43'52.45" on Mar 26.378, 7°42'43.89" on Mar 27.372) and Earth-Sun distance (log R 9.9995732, 9.9997037) from solar tables. The method uses epoch, mean motion, equation of centre, lunar/Venus/Jupiter perturbations and nutation/aberration terms.
results.modern_name: Solar ephemeris computation from tables (von Zach type tables, Seeberg meridian)

results.what: Preparatory solar data for redetermining the orbit of the comet of 1772 (later Biela's comet), in connection with the 1805 comet.
results.modern_name: Orbit determination of comet 1772 (3D/Biela), identity with the comet of 1805
results.usually_credited_to: Periodicity confirmed 1826 (Biela, Gambart, Clausen). Similarity of 1772 and 1805 noted in 1805-06 by Gauss, Bessel and others.

deep.surprise_reason: Purely routine numerical reduction of solar positions from tables for a comet-orbit computation. Gauss's 1805-06 involvement with the 1772/1805 comet is known; the page only documents his working method and self-corrections.

checkable.asserts: Obs. 1 mean longitude: epoch + day motion + hour motion = 4°48'5.49" (mod 360°)
Equals 3548.33 arcsec = 59'8.33", the Sun's mean daily motion
≈ 27.375 units/day ≈ 10000/365.26, so the 7383.22 column is the anomaly in 1/10000 circle

transcription_corrections: '0,9998494' should read '0,9990494' (overwritten digits). The tabular radius vector must be about 0.99905 to give 0.9990177 and to differ from obs. 2 by 0.000287.
'-135' (third correction to R, obs. 1) is overwritten; the final value requires '-115'.
'Long. ☉ 6° 43' 46,82 / 52,45': 46.82 is cancelled, the final value is 52.45".
'+ 5' [-49-] 10,3': 49" is cancelled and replaced by 10.3"; similarly 'März 27 8.55.[-49-] 27,3'.
In the obs. 2 radius side calculation, '+ 1098,9 / - 2,9' are interpolation increments applied to 0,9992269, giving 0,9993365.
